column2: The first conditional clause keeps the husband's finding of an unseemly thing, written certificate delivered into her hands, and dismissal, rather than treating it as a detached command to divorce.
The woman's departure and marriage to another man continue the conditional sequence.
The second husband's dismissal with a delivered certificate or his death are alternative intervening circumstances.
The prohibition concerns the former husband's taking her back after the intervening marriage; defilement and the land prohibition remain explicit.
The newly married man is free from war and duty for one year, and he is to gladden his wife; the direction of that action is retained.
Both mill and upper stone are protected from pledging, with life itself as the stated reason.
Kidnapping an Israelite brother, subjugating him and selling him remain in the case leading to the thief's death.
The repeated taking heed and the Levitical priests' instruction govern the affliction called lepra.
column3: Leprosy is retained as traditional vocabulary, without claiming identity with a single modern medical diagnosis.

column2: Miriam's treatment on the journey out of Egypt remains the named warning.
The broadly stated debt does not authorize the creditor to enter the debtor's house for the pledge.
The creditor waits outside while the debtor himself brings out the pledge.
The poor man's pledge must not remain with the creditor overnight; in your keeping makes the implied possession intelligible.
The emphatic return at sunset allows the poor man to sleep and bless; eleemosyne remains mercy rather than being harmonized to righteousness.
column3: The contextual rendering of eleemosyne as mercy should be assessed with 6:25 in later lexical review.

column2: The prohibition on withholding wages covers both poor and needy brethren and resident sojourners.
Same-day payment, sunset, poverty and hope in the wages remain. En soi is rendered in you, consistent with 23:22-23, rather than upon you.
column3: The selected negative future concerning the worker's outcry followed by the sin clause has a difficult logical connection. Inherited lest is a contextual rendering, not a literal representation of the conjunctions; this remains open.

column2: The reciprocal exclusions of vicarious execution lead to each person's own sin, preserving the fathers/children and sons/fathers wording.
Sojourner, orphan and widow all appear in the justice protection; the widow's garment has a separate pledge prohibition.
Household slavery in Egypt and redemption from there explain the command.
The forgotten sheaf must remain for four named groups, including the poor before sojourner, orphan and widow.
The olive gleaning prohibition includes the selected Egyptian-slavery reminder within this same unit, not only at 24:22.
Remaining grapes belong to the sojourner, orphan and widow; the repeated recipient list is not compressed.
The Egyptian-slavery reminder is repeated here as in the selected text, despite its earlier occurrence in 24:20.
Justifying the righteous and condemning the ungodly remain actions of judges in the stated dispute, preserving their judicial setting.
The selected action seats the offender before the judges; the number of blows is related to his ungodliness.
Forty is the stated limit, with no substitution of thirty-nine, and dishonouring one's brother supplies the reason against excess.
The ox is not to be muzzled while threshing, preserving the action rather than importing a later application.
Brothers dwelling together, death without seed, exclusion of an unrelated husband and the surviving brother's marital duty remain together.
The selected child, without an added firstborn restriction, is established in the dead man's name so that his name remains in Israel.
The woman's complaint repeats her husband's brother as subject in both clauses; neither refusal statement is omitted.
The elders summon and address the man, who then stands by his refusal to take her.
One sandal is removed and spitting is in his face; the refusal to build his brother's house explains the public response.
The household designation refers to the loosed sandal, retaining the selected naming formula.
The intervention is by the wife of one combatant to rescue her husband, with the anatomical object explicitly testicles.
Cutting off her hand and the refusal to spare are both retained without softening the stated penalty.
The selected e links great or small; revise and to or while retaining differing weights as the contextual rendering of the repeated weight noun.
column3: The force of weight and weight with the following disjunction merits fuller idiom review; this proposal preserves the selected conjunction without asserting exhaustive alignment.

column2: The corresponding measure prohibition likewise uses great or small; apply the same conjunction correction as at 25:13.
Both true and just qualify weight and measure, followed by the promise of long days in the given land.
The repetition everyone who does these things/everyone who does injustice remains, connecting the abomination to conduct.
Amalek's action on the journey out of Egypt is the explicit object of remembrance.
The attack reaches the weary rear; Israel is hungry and weary, whereas the final lack of fear of God concerns Amalek.
Rest from surrounding enemies precedes blotting out Amalek's name, not substituting memory for name; the final prohibition on forgetting remains.
Entry, inheritance and residence introduce the firstfruits instruction in sequence.
The firstfruits go into a basket and then to the chosen place where the divine name is called upon.
The speaker addresses the priest and refers to the Lord my God; the oath was to our fathers to give us the land.
The priest takes the basket from the worshipper's hands and places it before the altar.
My father forsook Syria preserves the selected Greek rather than replacing it with a wandering Aramean; the repeated greatness of nation and multitude remains.
Affliction, humiliation and hard labours are distinct actions imposed by the Egyptians.
The Lord hears the cry and sees humiliation, toil and distress, with all three objects retained.
The Lord Himself, great strength, mighty hand, His uplifted arm, great visions, signs and wonders all remain in the deliverance account.
Arrival at this place and the gift of the milk-and-honey land are both stated.
The direct prayer uses Thou and O Lord; the following instruction returns to ordinary you. The selected repeated milk-and-honey description is retained.
Rejoicing extends to the household, Levite and sojourner, in the good things given by the Lord.
The third year explicitly concerns the second tithe in the selected Greek; all four recipient groups eat and are filled.
The confession clears holy things from the house and gives them to four groups; direct address uses Thy and Thou, with both non-transgression and non-forgetting retained.
Mourning, unclean use and giving to the dead are separately negated; the confession shifts from the Lord my God to direct Thou as the Greek does.
column3: The ritual sense of ekarposa and its relation to unclean use needs specialist lexical review; inherited offered is provisional, not a settled technical gloss.

column2: The prayer distinguishes Thy people, land given them, our fathers and the land given us; these pronouns are not regularized.
The command to keep and do these ordinances and judgments requires all heart and all soul.
The people choose God to be their God, with walking, keeping and hearing as coordinated obligations; no absent Lord title is inserted here.
The Lord's choosing the people answers their choosing God, with possession and all His commandments retained.
The selected renowned, a boast and glorious remain the terms of distinction above the nations, ending in being a holy people as spoken.
